scope: One signed JPEG amplitude extension primitive, two native-input repeats and one affected owned-input screen. Two frozen JPEGs use one existing original 513x259 raster. No new image, preparation or quality enumeration.
changedPrimitive: After unchanged ReadBits admission and input traversal, subtract the exact category threshold, derive a sign mask, and apply the T.81 amplitude offset without a payload-dependent branch. Count zero retains its early return. No change to coefficient/Huffman parsing, categories, predictor/run bounds, marker handling, source positions, partial writes, cancellation or work. No new table/buffer/cache/dependency/unsafe code.

baseline.boundary: Identical resident prepared 8-bit 4:4:4 JPEG to independent owned RGBA8. Public managed Decode, allocation and disposal; native software mjpeg decoder, per-operation state reset, full-range BT.601 conversion, owned output allocation and release. Native context/conversion/input packet/frame wrappers reused; every call decodes and converts all pixels. Padded native rows are exposed without a gratuitous packing copy. Startup, I/O, IPC, generation, hashing, checks and tight-row file writes excluded. No encoder quality search or additional source raster. Decoder RGB maximum 4/RMSE 1.5, exact opaque alpha.

provenance: Frozen prepared native qscale-5 JPEG from HorizontalFlipInput.Create(8), original deterministic asymmetric RGBA8 flattened once on RGB 0x204060. 133041 bytes, common 1x2 factors (4:4:4) and variable Huffman tables. No additional source raster, upstream corpus or quality enumeration.

baselineCpuProfile.scope: Separate current fused-magnitude NativeDecode8 warm JPEG CPU sampling; workload loops include warmup/calibration. Not parity timing.
baselineCpuProfile.attributionRule: Match method names before the first parenthesis; parameter type names are excluded. coefficientEntropyGroup is the union of coefficient, reader and Huffman methods, not one primitive.

uncertainty: Short screens guide ranking and do not certify uniform parity. Ratios use the faster native bracket. Conservative uppers retain managed and native sample uncertainty; a nonpositive denominator is unbounded. The owned input has one affected screen. Failed post-run quiet samples and later passing cooldowns are retained. The baseline CPU profile precedes this primitive and is not candidate attribution.
